prompt.context: Our client, DigiBooks, is a manufacturer and seller of electronic book readers. DigiBooks also distributes e-books for the e-reader through their website. The reader is only compatible with books sold through the DigiBooks site. DigiBooks is planning the launch of its e-book readers in a country where no e-book readers are currently sold. Only 1% of the population has ever used an e-book reader, though 50% is aware of the concept. The Chief Marketing Officer of DigiBooks has come to you to help determine how DigiBooks should launch and market the e-reader product in this new country.
prompt.question: How should DigiBooks launch and market the e-reader product in this new country?

clarifying_info.q: What type of product is the e-reader?
clarifying_info.a: It is a software, hardware and network platform that utilizes wireless connectivity to enable users to shop for, download, browse, and read e-books, newspapers, magazines, blogs, and other digital media.

clarifying_info.q: What are the technical specs of DigiBooks' product?
clarifying_info.a: It uses an e-ink electronic paper display that features 16 shades of grey, allowing for a 12-hour battery life and easy readability.

clarifying_info.q: Has DigiBooks sold products outside the US before?
clarifying_info.a: No, DigiBooks has never sold a product outside of the US.

clarifying_info.q: Are there competitors in this new market?
clarifying_info.a: No competitors in the e-book or tablet space plan to enter this country.

exhibits.title: Market Segments
exhibits.shows: A table of three customer segments with their segment size and e-reader price point

exhibits.title: Channel Decisions
exhibits.shows: A table comparing Retail and Internet sales channels across four metrics: percent of total potential market, e-book gross margin %, e-reader gross margin %, penetration rate, and initial investment

framework: Segmentation, Targeting & Positioning: Identify which customer segments exist and which is most attractive (size, revenue potential, willingness to pay)
Product: Assess whether existing product fits local needs or requires adaptation
Price: Determine willingness to pay per segment; consider razor/blade model (low reader price, margin on e-books)
Promotion: Identify marketing mechanisms and channels to build awareness and drive trial
Place / Distribution: Evaluate retail vs. internet vs. alternative channels
Content Selection: Assess availability and breadth of e-book titles relevant to this country's readers

questions.prompt: Using a 3-year projection and Exhibit 1, which segment should DigiBooks target? (Note: the average price of an e-book is $10 for all segments; e-books and e-reader carry the same margin; assume all reader sales happen immediately and ignore TVM.)
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate 3-year revenue potential for each segment by combining e-reader revenue and e-book revenue, then multiply by segment size. The largest revenue potential drives the recommendation.

math.setup: Revenue per person = (books/year x $10/book x 3 years) + (1 e-reader x price). Total Revenue = Revenue per person x Segment size.
math.answer: Target the Occasional Reader (OR) segment with a 3-year revenue potential of $8.5B, the highest of the three segments.

questions.prompt: DigiBooks is considering whether to sell e-readers through retail stores or through the internet. How would you evaluate this decision?
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure a pros/cons analysis for each channel across dimensions such as margin, trial/discovery, marketing synergies, customer service, and cost/speed to establish.

questions.prompt: DigiBooks has decided to price the e-reader at $100 and target the Occasional Reader segment. Using Exhibit 2, estimate the 1-year gross profit (after initial investment) for each sales channel. Which channel should DigiBooks choose?
questions.guidance: Candidate should compute gross profit from both e-book and e-reader sales for each channel, apply penetration to the OR segment size (20M x 50% of market served by each channel = 10M addressable per channel), then subtract the initial investment. A strong answer clearly lays out the table before computing.

math.setup: Addressable customers per channel = 20M OR segment x 50% share = 10M. Gross Profit = [(10 books x $10/book x ebook_GM%) + ($100/e-reader x ereader_GM%)] x (10M x penetration%) - initial investment.
math.answer: Retail channel yields $300M gross profit vs. Internet at $100M. Choose Retail.

recommendation: DigiBooks should launch the e-reader targeting the Occasional Reader segment through the Retail sales channel
The Retail channel is projected to generate $300M gross profit in year 1 on a $20M initial investment
risks: No prior international experience — operational and logistics risks in a new country
Retail channel requires time and money to establish and training costs for retail staff
Low current usage (1%) means heavy investment in consumer education and trial generation
Potential future competitor entry could erode first-mover advantage
next_steps: Determine advertising and promotional mechanisms appropriate for this country
Decide whether to manufacture locally or source from existing US facilities
Monitor for competitor entry and prepare contingency plans
Assess e-book content availability and library breadth for this market
